candidate_method_families: domain-local Hurwitz/Rouche zero transport on the minimal root-relevant strip
weighted-L1 or source-specific transform-continuity bridge from ground-state error to compact-uniform complex Fourier/Mellin error
lowest-eigenspace perturbation with quantitative spectral separation or alternate rigidity
source-specific QW_lambda/prolate trace-formula bridge without generic operator-norm assumptions
hostile small-gap and growing-domain norm-loss calibrations before target-specific theorem search
tool_applicability_notes: The Hurwitz tool is selected only for the target-side implication: once a source-defined cofinal family has finite-stage off-real zero exclusion and locally uniform convergence to exact nonzero Xi on every compact subset of the open strip |Im z|<1/2, the tool transports zero exclusion there. It supplies no source-side ground-state/proxy estimate.

DifferenceWitness from the parent calibration: RH-SPEC-002a no longer asks which generic convergence topology is sufficient. It asks how the actual CCM semilocal ground state xi_lambda can be related to the explicit proxy k_lambda strongly enough to meet the selected tool's preconditions.
failure_reuse_notes: F-RH-SPEC-002-FINITE-ZERO-PREFIX warns that zeros or one-point normalization do not control the zero-free/growth factor; therefore c_lambda and the transform norm must be source-defined before comparing with Xi.
F-RH-SPEC-002-JOINT-LIMIT-AMBIGUITY requires keeping fixed-lambda N->infinity transport separate from the lambda->infinity proxy bridge unless a uniform joint-limit theorem is proved.

F-RH-SPEC-002-STRONG-RESOLVENT-INCOMPLETE and F-RH-SPEC-002-GALERKIN-POLLUTION warn against substituting generic operator convergence for the exact ground-state transform bridge. They do not prove the CCM family fails.

Cheapest repeat-failure regressions for any candidate are: a nearly degenerate self-adjoint 2x2 family testing residual-to-eigenvector stability, and a growing-domain function family testing whether the proposed source norm truly controls compact-uniform complex transform error.
unresolved_warnings: CCM explicitly leave simplicity/evenness of the semilocal QW_lambda ground state open; RH-SPEC-002a treats it as a sibling dependency rather than an assumption silently consumed by the proxy bridge.
The source proves k_lambda transform convergence to Xi on closed substrips but does not prove k_lambda approximates a scalar multiple of xi_lambda strongly enough for zero transport.
Qualitative simplicity without quantitative spectral separation may be insufficient for perturbative eigenspace stability.
Unweighted L2 proximity on a lambda-dependent growing logarithmic interval may not control complex transforms uniformly on a strip.
A source-side scalar normalization c_lambda must not be fitted to known zeta zeros or chosen after seeing Xi discrepancy.
Success of the lambda-stage ground-state/proxy bridge would not discharge fixed-lambda finite-N determinant/eigenvector transport.
evidence_pointers: Alain Connes, Caterina Consani, Henri Moscovici, Zeta Spectral Triples, arXiv:2511.22755 (2025), Lemma 7.3 and Section 8
